newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says thinks Hokkaido banks' merger to proceed.
newsitem.headline: MOF says thinks Hokkaido banks' merger to proceed.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) does not think the planned merger of Hokkaido Takushoku Bank and Hokkaido Bank, set to take place next April, will falter, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Tuesday.
Mitsuzuka said the two banks were in close contact and were cooperating with each other, with the aim of achieving a merger in April.
"I do not think at all that this (the planned merger) will fall apart," he said.
He also said the ministry thought the merger into a regional bank was the best route for the two banks to pursue.

The banks announced in April of this year a plan to merge next April, but earlier this month Hokkaido Bank, a regional bank, said that the merger with city bank Hokkaido Takushoku Bank could be delayed if the two could not come up with business rationalisation plans by the end of September.
